title: Austerity
note: He defines austerity as bearing the pain of vows, such as cutting food and standing in sun, rain and cold so the mind won’t follow the senses, while tending other beings. It comes once refusing meat has ripened compassion.

couplets.plain: To bear the pain that comes to you and cause no pain to any living being: that is the form of austerity.
couplets.pm: The form of austerity is just this much: bearing the pains that come to your own soul from cutting food and the like, and causing no pain to other living beings. All else falls within these two.
couplets.sensitive: makes enduring suffering the whole of discipline

links.quote: that is the form of austerity
links.reason: Reduces the whole of austerity to bearing pain and causing no pain.

links.quote: cause no pain to any living being
links.reason: Not hurting any living thing is half of what austerity is said to be.

couplets.plain: Austerity comes to those who have austerity. For those without it, taking it up is in vain.
couplets.pm: Not only its fruit but austerity itself comes only to those with austerity from a former life. For those without that, taking it up is wasted effort. The former have the knowledge and strength of long practice and see it through. The others lack these and don’t.

links.quote: taking it up is in vain
links.reason: Sets the test of austerity: those without it gain nothing by taking it up.

couplets.plain: Have the others forgotten austerity, in their wish to provide for those who have renounced?
couplets.pm: Those who stay in household life, wishing to give renouncers food, medicine and shelter, seem to have forgotten austerity, so great is their love of their own giving. Austerity yields all you wish, so everyone would otherwise do it. It follows that austerity ranks above giving.

links.reason: Teases everyone else for dropping austerity as if providing for renouncers excused them.

couplets.plain: Crushing enemies and raising those who are dear: if you wish it, austerity can do both.
couplets.pm: If those who do austerity so think, its power will destroy those who harm their practice and raise those who delight in it. “If” shows that by nature they don’t think this. A true renouncer has no friends or enemies, so the power is credited to the austerity. Ruin or gain comes at a thought.

links.reason: Claims for austerity the power to crush enemies and raise those who are dear.

couplets.plain: Because what you want comes as you want it, austerity is striven for here.
couplets.pm: If you strive, you can have the fruits you want in the next life, just as you want them. So the wise strive at austerity in this life. The higher states and liberation can’t be reached without it.

links.quote: what you want comes as you want it
links.reason: Gives the reason people strive at austerity: it grants every wish exactly as wished.

couplets.plain: Those who do austerity do their own work. The rest are caught in craving and do what is in vain.
couplets.pm: Only those who renounce and do austerity do their own work. All who pursue wealth and pleasure are caught in the net of craving and harm themselves. Austerity brings a soul long afflicted by birth, disease, age and death to knowledge and liberation. Momentary pleasure earns sin that brings suffering in many births.

links.quote: Those who do austerity do their own work
links.reason: Only those doing austerity are said to be truly minding their own work.
Everyone else is caught in craving, doing what comes to nothing.

couplets.plain: Like gold that shines brighter the more it is burned, those who can endure shine brighter the more pain burns them.
couplets.pm: Gold melted in the fire loses its impurity and shines more, the more it burns. In the same way, the more the pain of austerity afflicts those who can do it, the more their sin falls away and their knowledge grows. Knowledge is called light because it shows things as light does.

links.quote: shine brighter the more pain burns them
gold that shines brighter the more it is burned

couplets.plain: All other living beings worship someone who has wholly won their own soul.
couplets.pm: All living beings that haven’t done so worship someone who has gained their soul for themselves. That means doing their own work, austerity, and nothing is harder to gain. The others are those caught in craving. They worship because such a person has the power to curse and to bless.

links.reason: All other beings worship the one who has wholly won their own soul.

couplets.plain: Those who have reached the strength that comes from austerity can even leap past death.
couplets.pm: Getting past death itself is possible for those who have gained the power that comes from austerity. “Even” shows how hard this is, or else means that this comes as well as being worshipped by all. The power is to curse and to bless.

couplets.plain: Why are so many people without? Because few do austerity and many don’t.
couplets.pm: Why are the rich of the world few and the poor many? Because those who do austerity are few and those who don’t are many. Wealth and poverty here also stand for having understanding and lacking it. Those who don’t do austerity have no joy even in this life.
couplets.sensitive: blames poverty on lack of discipline

links.quote: few do austerity and many don’t
links.reason: Explains the world’s want by how few take up austerity.

ideaLinks.quote: cause no pain to any living being
ideaLinks.reason: Causing no pain is one of the two things that make up the whole of austerity.

ideaLinks.quote: Those who do austerity do their own work. The rest are caught in craving
ideaLinks.reason: Those who do austerity serve their own good while the rest are caught in craving.
